_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Pidilite Industries (consolidated, ₹ crore). Segment-driven revenue on the company's two reported segments, Consumer & Bazaar (C&B) and Business to Business (B2B), plus 'Others' (raw-material sales, NBFC), each on net revenue after inter-segment sales so that the three sum to reported revenue. Segment margin = segment EBITDA (segment result + allocable depreciation, consolidated segment note) as % of net revenue. Corporate costs not allocated to segments (unallocable expenses net of unallocable depreciation, as reconciled to Screener EBITDA) are a separate line. Treasury income = yield × opening cash and investments less borrowings. Valued on P/E, as the street does.

segments.name: Consumer & Bazaar
segments._why: FY27 +18%: Q1 standalone C&B revenue +22.5% (UVG 12.2%, i.e. ~10% from price and mix after blended price rises of ~4-5% in mid-April and ~7-8% in early May 2026). Price stays in the base until Apr-May 2027, but management expects to pass back some of it as rebates because VAM fell sharply from its ~US$1,800-2,000/t peak; we assume UVG ~10.5% plus ~7.5% price for the year (Q2 high-teens, H2 low-teens). FY28 +11%: price laps and turns slightly negative; UVG ~11% (management: double-digit UVG, 'about 100 bps' of yearly improvement is the aim, FY26 11.1%). FY29 +12%: UVG ~11% plus ~1% price.
segments._marginWhy: Consolidated C&B segment EBITDA margin was 29.1% (FY24), 30.9% (FY25) and 33.0% (FY26) on benign input costs. Q1FY27 standalone C&B PBIT margin rose 211bp YoY (low-cost inventory, proactive pricing, lower schemes), but management said Q2 would absorb high-cost inventory and some price would be passed back. We take 32.2% in FY27 and 32.4% in FY28-29: a little below FY26 and well above the FY22-23 inflation years (26.6%/23.4%).

segments.name: Business to Business
segments._why: FY27 +12%: Q1 standalone B2B revenue +16.0% (UVG 7.3%: domestic projects/industrial UVG +10.4%, exports UVG −8.4% on West Asia disruption); domestic B2B subsidiaries (Nina waterproofing etc.) grew only 3.4%. We assume exports stay weak through FY27. FY28 +10% / FY29 +11%: domestic projects (Pidilite Professional Solutions) and industrial adhesives grow double digit; exports recover partly.
segments._marginWhy: Consolidated B2B segment EBITDA margin 17.0% (FY24), 20.6% (FY25), 20.1% (FY26); 9.9-12.7% in FY22-23 when input costs spiked. Pigment exports are the most cyclical part. 19.5% in FY27 (input costs, weak exports), 20% after.

segments.name: Others (raw-material sales, NBFC)
segments._why: Small and erratic (₹39-102 cr a year since FY21); held flat.
segments._marginWhy: Segment result between −₹9 cr and +₹6 cr in FY21-26; held at zero.

_unallocLabel: Corporate costs not allocated to segments (sum of segment EBITDA less Screener EBITDA)
_unallocWhy: Sum of segment EBITDA less reported (Screener) EBITDA: ₹353 cr (FY21, 4.8% of revenue), ₹583 cr (FY24, 4.7%), ₹750 cr (FY25, 5.7%), ₹871 cr (FY26, 6.0%). It is mostly corporate overheads, central brand/A&P and new-category costs (paints, electronics, Unofin). We hold it at ~6.0% of revenue: ₹1,020 / 1,130 / 1,260 cr.
_capexWhy: Management: capex runs at 3-5% of revenue (8-May-2026 call); FY26 ~₹570 cr per management (₹593 cr on Screener's cash flow), FY25 ₹452 cr. CRISIL (2-Sep-2026) expects ₹750-850 cr a year over the medium term (new white-glue plant in West India commissioning in Q1FY27, tile-adhesive and construction-chemical plants, automation). ₹750 / 800 / 850 cr ≈ 4.4% / 4.2% / 4.0% of revenue.
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹395 cr ≈ 4.8% of average gross block (₹8,165 cr, which includes the Araldite brand and other acquired intangibles); Q1FY27 ₹97 cr (₹388 cr annualised).
_treasuryWhy: Applied to opening cash and investments less borrowings (₹3,433 cr at Mar-25, ₹4,232 cr at Mar-26 on Screener). FY26 other income ₹248 cr incl. −₹18 cr exceptional = ~7.7% of opening net cash before exceptionals; Q4FY26 was hit by mark-to-market losses as bond yields rose, Q1FY27 ₹95 cr before a +₹14 cr exceptional. 7% a year.
_interestLabel: Interest cost (mainly leases and subsidiaries' working-capital lines)
_interestWhy: FY26 ₹54 cr; Q1FY27 ₹13 cr. Standalone is debt free (CRISIL); ₹417 cr of borrowings incl. leases at Mar-26.
_taxWhy: FY26 effective rate 25.6% (₹849 cr on ₹3,320 cr PBT, AR note 46); Q1FY27 ~26%. 25.5% (new regime 25.2% plus non-deductibles).
_payoutWhy: FY26 regular dividend ₹11.50 a share (48.9% of profit before exceptionals per the company) plus a one-off special ₹5 (B K Parekh centenary); 45-49% in FY23-25. 50% ahead.

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash, branded consumer franchise with steady volumes; below-market sensitivity (Ke 11.3%).
dcf._tgWhy: India's nominal GDP grows ~10%; a dominant domestic brand franchise can grow near nominal GDP for long, but we stay at the top of the house 5-6% range: 6%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~12% to 9% by year 15: underpenetrated waterproofing and tile adhesives keep growth above GDP for a decade, core adhesives grow at 1-2x real GDP.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: From ~24% towards 23%, the upper half of management's 20-24% corridor: input-cost cycles recur.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~4% of revenue towards 3.5%, within management's 3-5% band.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Price rises stick while VAM falls back (no rebates), UVG runs at 12-13% as urban demand stays buoyant and waterproofing/tile adhesives take share; exports recover in FY28; C&B margin holds near 34% and consolidated EBITDA margin settles around 25%, above the top of management's corridor.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Price give-backs come faster than input relief, inflation compresses demand (UVG falls to 7-8%), competition from cement and tile makers in tile adhesives and from Asian Paints/JSW in waterproofing intensifies, exports stay weak; C&B margin slips towards 30% and consolidated EBITDA margin to ~21.5%, the middle of the corridor.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Pidilite (Motilal Oswal 50x FY28E EPS, Prabhudas Lilladher 50x Jun-28E EPS, Aug-2026). 45x = Pidilite's ~64x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021, cut by the ~27% median de-rating of six consumer and building-material peers versus their five-year median P/E by 30-Sep-2026 (≈47x), and by ~4% more because our FY26-29E EPS growth (~14% a year) is below the ~17% of FY21-26 and comes off peak-range margins. Bull 55x (its 25th-percentile forward P/E since 2021), bear 40x (its 10th percentile since 2016).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts net cash at face value. 31x Sep-28E EBITDA = Pidilite's ~56x median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021, less the same ~27% sector de-rating (≈41x trailing), restated for Sep-28E EBITDA being ~27% above the twelve months to Jun-26 (≈32x), less the same ~4% growth discount.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, Ke 11.3%, terminal growth 6%, plus net cash.
